To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

practical pre-aggregation can be extended to cover a wide range of real-world situations by using simple transformations on dimension hierarchies, fact-dimension relationships and aggregate queries, and that these transformations can be performed with low computational complexity.
“Practical pre-aggregation is feasible in many more cases than previously thought.”

(1) the practical pre-aggregation approach to speeding up OLAP queries can be significantly extended to cover a much larger set of realistic situations than previously possible, (2) the extensions are achieved by transforming dimension hierarchies, fact-dimension relationships and OLAP structures in a systematic manner to make them suitable for preaggregation, and (3) the transformations can be done efficiently and incrementally to minimize the cost of updating the OLAP structures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
making practical preaggregation a practical reality.
the design of OLAP structures that support practical pre-aggregation for a broad class of realistic OLAP applications, which was not possible in the past.
the practical application of pre-aggregation, which has been a largely theoretical subject in the past.

the algorithms described in this paper provide a general and practical solution to the problem of practical pre-aggregations for a large and realistic class of OLAP structures.
the proposed approach is an effective and practical way to extend the scope of practical aggregation to a much larger range of realistic situations than is currently possible.
the algorithms presented in this paper are a significant contribution to the field of OLAP.

practical pre-aggregation can be applied to a much broader range of applications than was previously believed.
